lesson.title: Adding a Two-Digit and a One-Digit Number
lesson.subject: math

contentBlocks.text: You can break numbers apart and compare them. Today: use tens and ones to add a bigger number and a smaller number together.

To add a two-digit number and a one-digit number, keep the tens the same and just add to the ones. For example, 23 + 5: the '2 tens' stays put, and you just add 3 ones + 5 ones = 8 ones, giving 28. Try 41 + 6: keep the 4 tens, add 1 one + 6 ones = 7 ones, giving 47. Solve 35 + 3 and 62 + 7 the same way.
You just added two-digit numbers using your tens and ones understanding! Tomorrow we'll review everything from this week.

objectives: Add a two-digit number and a one-digit number by keeping the tens constant and adding the ones
Solve two-digit-plus-one-digit addition problems without regrouping
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review comparing two-digit numbers from yesterday.
2. Introduce the tens-stay-put, ones-add strategy using 23+5.
3. Practice 41+6 together.
4. Have the child solve 35+3 and 62+7 independently.
5. Complete the worksheet.
6. Preview tomorrow's cumulative review.
differentiationTips: Struggling: use physical ten-bundles and loose ones objects to model each addition problem concretely
Ready for more: ask the child what would happen if the ones added up to 10 or more (a preview of regrouping, saved for a future lesson)
This lesson deliberately avoids regrouping (carrying) — every problem is designed so the ones sum stays under 10
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Directly addresses Common Core Grade 1 standard 1.NBT.4: adding within 100 using concrete models and strategies based on place value, without regrouping.
